if (nrow(evaluation) != 1L) stop("Expected exactly one selected FIA evaluation record.")
evaluation_id <- format(evaluation$evalid[[1]], scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)

effect_row <- function(effect_label, required = FALSE) {
  result <- odds |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$label == .env$effect_label) |>
    dplyr::slice_head(n = 1)
  if (required && nrow(result) != 1L) stop("Required model effect not found: ", effect_label)
  result
}
format_effect <- function(effect) {
  sprintf(
    "OR %.2f, 95%% CI %.2f–%.2f",
    effect$estimate[[1]], effect$conf.low[[1]], effect$conf.high[[1]]
  )
}

maple_effect <- effect_row("Sugar maple basal area", required = TRUE)
coverage_effect <- effect_row("Microplot condition coverage", required = TRUE)
temperature_effect <- effect_row("Mean annual temperature")
precipitation_effect <- effect_row("Annual precipitation")
age_effect <- effect_row("Stand age")
disturbance_effect <- effect_row("Recorded disturbance")

climate_statements <- character()
if (nrow(temperature_effect)) {
  climate_statements <- c(
    climate_statements,
    paste0("The temperature proxy had ", format_effect(temperature_effect), ".")
  )
}
if (nrow(precipitation_effect)) {
  climate_statements <- c(
    climate_statements,
    paste0("The precipitation proxy had ", format_effect(precipitation_effect), ".")
  )
}
climate_text <- if (length(climate_statements)) {
  paste(
    "The retained county-scale climate terms described a broad geographic gradient.",
    paste(climate_statements, collapse = " "),
    "These coefficients must not be read as plot-level climate effects."
  )
} else {
  "County-scale climate terms were not retained by the pre-specified support and correlation checks."
}

other_effects <- dplyr::bind_rows(age_effect, disturbance_effect)
null_other_effects <- other_effects |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$conf.low <= 1, .data$conf.high >= 1) |>
  dplyr::pull(.data$label)
other_effects_text <- if (!nrow(other_effects)) {
  "Stand age and recorded disturbance were not retained by the data-support checks."
} else if (length(null_other_effects)) {
  paste0(
    "The 95% confidence intervals crossed one for ",
    paste(tolower(null_other_effects), collapse = " and "), "."
  )
} else {
  "The retained stand age or disturbance intervals did not cross one."
}

fixed_effect_text <- paste(odds$label, collapse = ", ")
cohort_n <- function(step_name) {
  value <- cohort$observations[cohort$step == step_name]
  if (length(value) != 1L) stop("Cohort step not found: ", step_name)
  scales::comma(value)
}

## Abstract {.unnumbered}

This exploratory study evaluated `r scales::comma(summary$plot_conditions)` northern-hardwood plot-condition measurements from `r summary$counties` Michigan counties. It asked whether places with substantial established sugar maple also showed evidence of the next cohort. Sugar-maple seedlings were tallied in `r scales::percent(summary$maple_seedling_detected / summary$seedling_sampled, accuracy = 0.1)` of conditions with demonstrated microplot sampling opportunity. A transparent, sample-relative indicator flagged `r scales::comma(summary$potential_gaps)` observations (`r scales::percent(summary$potential_gap_fraction, accuracy = 0.1)`) combining upper-third sugar-maple basal-area share with no sugar-maple seedlings tallied. Associations were evaluated with `r support$model_type`. Results describe the analyzed sample and do not constitute FIA design-based population estimates or causal effects.

## Why regeneration matters

Northern hardwood forests can retain a mature sugar-maple canopy even when younger cohorts are sparse. That mismatch is relevant to future composition, but it does not by itself identify a mechanism. Browsing, competition, site conditions, management history, disturbance, seed availability, and sampling variability can all contribute.

This project therefore asks a deliberately bounded question:

> Among contemporary Michigan FIA northern-hardwood observations, which stand and broad-scale climate characteristics are associated with whether sugar-maple seedlings were tallied?

## Data

:::: {.columns .source-grid .column-page}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Forest Inventory and Analysis

The analysis uses the Michigan SQLite release from the U.S. Forest Service FIA DataMart [@usfs_datamart]. FIA reference tables—not undocumented numeric constants—identify sugar maple and the retained forest types. The analytical key is a plot visit and condition (`PLT_CN + CONDID`). TREE and SEEDLING records are aggregated independently before they are joined, preventing a tree-by-seedling Cartesian product.

FIA plot coordinates are legally protected. No public coordinates are plotted or treated as exact environmental locations. County identifiers supplied by FIA provide the spatial link used here.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Climate

Daymet Version 4 R1 provides daily 1-km temperature and precipitation estimates [@thornton2022daymet]. For each Michigan county, this analysis uses the Daymet cell at an interior representative location to construct a 1991–2020 climate normal. These values are broad county proxies, not plot-level measurements.
:::
::::

## Methods

::::: {.method-grid .column-page}
:::: {.method-card}
[01 · Resolve]{.method-label}

**Reference-driven cohort**

Species and forest types resolve from FIADB reference tables rather than hidden constants; the published release pins its documented evaluation identifier.
::::

:::: {.method-card}
[02 · Aggregate]{.method-label}

**Condition-level ecology**

TREE and SEEDLING records aggregate independently before joining at `PLT_CN + CONDID`.
::::

:::: {.method-card}
[03 · Enrich]{.method-label}

**Protected spatial link**

County identifiers connect 1991–2020 Daymet proxies without exposing or approximating protected plot locations.
::::

:::: {.method-card}
[04 · Estimate]{.method-label}

**Cluster-aware inference**

The supported logistic model carries county and plot-visit random intercepts plus transparent support gates.
::::
:::::

### Established sugar maple

For every live TREE record, basal-area contribution on the FIA plot basis is calculated as

$$
BA_i = 0.005454 \times DIA_i^2 \times TPA_{i,unadj},
$$

where diameter is in inches and the resulting contribution is in square feet per acre on the unadjusted sample basis. Condition-level densities use the recorded condition proportion. Sugar-maple basal-area share divides its live-tree contribution by the total live-tree contribution within the same condition.

As a calculation check, derived live-tree basal area agreed closely with FIA's condition-level `BALIVE` field across `r scales::comma(ba_check$observations)` conditions (Pearson *r* = `r round(ba_check$pearson_correlation, 3)`; mean absolute error `r round(ba_check$mean_absolute_error_ft2_ac, 2)` ft²/ac).

### Regeneration

SEEDLING `TPA_UNADJ` values are aggregated by species and plot-condition. The primary response is binary detection. A zero means no sugar-maple seedlings were tallied on sampled microplots; it is not proof that the entire condition lacked seedlings.

### Exploratory regeneration-gap indicator

The hero figure flags a **potential regeneration gap** when a condition has:

1. sugar-maple basal-area share in the upper third among conditions with demonstrated seedling sampling; and
2. no sugar-maple seedlings tallied.

The continuous companion indicator is the percentile rank of established share minus the percentile rank of log seedling density. Neither measure is presented as a validated ecological index.

### Model

The supported model is a `r support$model_type` with no-sugar-maple-seedlings-tallied as the response. Continuous predictors are standardized. Retained fixed effects were `r fixed_effect_text`. The fitted random-effects structure was `r support$random_effect_structure`. The model uses `r scales::comma(support$observations)` complete conditions from `r scales::comma(support$plot_visits)` plot visits across `r support$counties` counties; `r support$multi_condition_plot_visits` visits contributed more than one condition. There were `r round(support$events_per_term, 1)` outcome events per fixed-effect term. Odds ratios express associations with the odds of no seedlings being tallied.

::: {.table-panel .column-page}
```{r}
#| label: tbl-model-specification
#| tbl-cap: "Release model specification and support."
model_specification <- tibble::tibble(
  Item = c(
    "Formula", "Response events", "Response non-events", "Complete-case fraction",
    "Counties", "Plot visits", "Multi-condition plot visits", "Events per fixed term"
  ),
  Value = c(
    support$model_formula,
    scales::comma(support$events_no_seedlings),
    scales::comma(support$events_seedlings),
    scales::percent(support$complete_case_fraction, accuracy = 0.1),
    scales::comma(support$counties),
    scales::comma(support$plot_visits),
    scales::comma(support$multi_condition_plot_visits),
    sprintf("%.1f", support$events_per_term)
  )
)
knitr::kable(model_specification, align = c("l", "l"))
```

::: {.result-interpretation .column-page}
[Reading the model]{.result-interpretation-label}

Higher established sugar-maple basal area was associated with lower odds of no seedlings being tallied: a one-standard-deviation increase in log basal area corresponded to an odds ratio of `r sprintf("%.2f", maple_effect$estimate)` (95% CI `r sprintf("%.2f", maple_effect$conf.low)`–`r sprintf("%.2f", maple_effect$conf.high)`). Greater microplot condition coverage was also associated with lower non-detection odds (OR `r sprintf("%.2f", coverage_effect$estimate)`, 95% CI `r sprintf("%.2f", coverage_effect$conf.low)`–`r sprintf("%.2f", coverage_effect$conf.high)`), reinforcing why sampling opportunity belongs in the model.

`r climate_text` `r other_effects_text`
:::

## Discussion

:::: {.interpretation-grid .column-page}
::: {.interpretation-card .interpretation-supported}
[What the evidence supports]{.interpretation-kicker}

- A transparent screen for canopy–cohort mismatch in the analyzed sample.
- Adjusted associations with seedling non-detection under the supported model.
- Reproducible hypotheses for field or design-based follow-up.
:::

::: {.interpretation-card .interpretation-boundary}
[What it does not establish]{.interpretation-kicker}

- Statewide prevalence or formal FIA population estimates.
- A causal effect of canopy, climate, browsing, or disturbance.
- Exact plot-level climate exposure or long-term cohort survival.
:::
::::

The analysis makes the distinction between established live-tree basal area and observed seedling recruitment visible. Under the primary rule, `r summary$potential_gaps` of `r summary$seedling_sampled` sampled conditions were flagged. Raising the established-maple threshold from an upper-third share of `r scales::percent(thresholds$primary_established_threshold, accuracy = 0.1)` to an upper-quartile share of `r scales::percent(thresholds$sensitivity_established_threshold, accuracy = 0.1)` reduced the flag count to `r thresholds$sensitivity_gap_n` (`r scales::percent(thresholds$sensitivity_gap_fraction, accuracy = 0.1)`). This sensitivity is a reason to treat the flag as a screening device rather than a fixed ecological category.

The model estimates which measured stand and broad climate attributes covary with seedling detection after adjustment for the other retained terms. Confidence intervals—not prediction accuracy—are the primary evidence.

The results should be interpreted as hypotheses and patterns worthy of follow-up. A seedling tally is an imperfect window into recruitment, and seedlings do not guarantee survival into sapling or canopy cohorts.

## Limitations

1. **Protected locations.** County-scale climate and maps avoid treating public FIA coordinates as exact.
2. **Sampling opportunity.** A zero means no seedlings were tallied on sampled microplots, not ecological absence across the condition.
3. **Observational design.** Associations are not causal effects.
4. **Sample versus population.** `TPA_UNADJ` expands records within the plot design; it is not a statewide survey weight. Formal statewide estimates require FIA evaluation, stratum, adjustment, and sampling-error procedures [@bechtold2005sampling].
5. **Exploratory indicator.** The gap flag is sample-relative and threshold-dependent.
6. **Unmeasured drivers.** Deer browsing, soils, management history, competition, and other factors are incompletely represented.
7. **Temporal alignment.** Climate normals summarize 1991–2020 and do not reproduce weather immediately preceding each measurement.

::::

:::: {.repro-card}
[**renv**]{.repro-value}

locked R environment

:::::

Raw data are excluded from version control. Source URLs, cached-file retrieval timestamps, file sizes, and checksums—including each county's Daymet API response—are recorded in `outputs/audits/data-provenance.csv`. Important joins record row counts, unique keys, and unmatched keys. The public repository includes a curated [release validation record](https://github.com/dineshpotla/canopy-to-cohort/blob/main/outputs/audits/release-validation.csv) and [aggregate model-support evidence](https://github.com/dineshpotla/canopy-to-cohort/blob/main/outputs/tables/model-support.csv).

GitHub Actions runs the 11 data-free expectations and skips five derived-data/model tests by design. The completed v1.1.0 local build ran all 33 expectations. From a fresh clone, the full analysis runs with:

```bash
make setup
make acquire
make all
```

Package versions are recorded in `renv.lock`. The release was tested with R 4.6.1 and Quarto 1.9.38. FIA's state archive URL is mutable, so acquisition compares downloaded source sizes and SHA-256 hashes with the v1.0.0/v1.1.0 manifest and warns when a current-data rerun is not byte-identical to the published source snapshot.
